purpose: Held-out captured-footage test corpus. Genuinely camera-captured scenes, never used for training, checkpoint selection or hyperparameter tuning.
why_this_exists: Milestone 4.5's video benchmark was procedurally generated and its only positive result came from an adversarial zone plate, so no video claim survived. Synthetic proxies cannot answer a web-video question.
licence_policy: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain only, read from each file's own imageinfo. Sources are NOT redistributed: the fetcher pins URL and SHA-256 and a clone re-fetches.
independence: Video, from Commons video namespace. The training corpus is Wikimedia still images from the CC-Zero category; the Milestone 4.5 independent set is Met Museum stills. No overlap in medium or collection.

fetch_summary.note: Sources are gitignored and never redistributed; hashes pin what was used.

excluded_clips.reason: Burned-in telemetry HUD and a rendered OpenStreetMap inset with vector road lines and text labels. Independent review masked the four synthetic rectangles (11.5% of frame) and found 77%/95%/99% of this clip's advantage at high/typical/poor came from rendered pixels rather than captured ones - the same failure mode as Milestone 4.5's zone plate. Fails Part A.

Source decode corruption: a chroma-smeared vertical band grows from frame 9 to cover roughly the left 38% of frame 18, reproduced bit-for-bit from the pinned source, plus a large semi-transparent burned-in channel logo. Corrupt pixels are not valid ground truth.

9:16 vertical source: active picture is 1214 px wide, so fitting a 2560x1440 landscape master requires a 2.11x upscale. The resulting reference is interpolated rather than captured, which asks the model to recover detail the source never contained. Structurally unfit as an HR reference, independently of its score. Removed together with the other two faces clips from the same series.

exclusion_policy: Clips are removed for documented corpus-purity defects - synthetic overlays, corrupt source - never for their scores. Independent review verified the headline survives both with these clips included and excluded, and both are reported.
scope_limitation: Predominantly aerial, web-sourced 4K footage: 7 of 10 clips are aerial or airborne, several are Commons VP9 transcodes of YouTube deliveries rather than camera originals, lowlight is n=1 and texture n=2, and two clips carry very little motion. This corpus supports a claim about that population, not about captured video in general, and it contains no faces at all.
known_gaps: No faces/people category. The only permissively licensed face footage found at sufficient resolution was 9:16 vertical and could not supply a landscape HR master. Faces are therefore UNMEASURED in this milestone, not shown to be fine - and results/captured-faces-sensitivity.json records what the corpus said with those clips included, so the removal is auditable rather than quiet.
